title: Feature-flag rollout & client migration PRD for hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Aisha Raman
description: PRD to define the feature-flag driven rollout, client migration path, scope clarifications, and acceptance criteria for the consolidated hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: enable progressive exposure to the new unified surface while preserving behavior for existing clients and providing clear rollback and fallback behavior.
scope: Implement feature flags per-tenant for new unified endpoint surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank).
Client SDKs: add opt-in flag and client-side migration helper utilities for Node/Python/Go.
Server-side gateway: route flagged traffic to new handler with telemetry and canary percent controls.
Define acceptance telemetry and quality checks tied to eval prompt sets for generation/embedding consistency.
Automated rollback triggers based on SLO/quality regressions and cost thresholds.
out_of_scope: Large-scale SDK refactor unrelated to migration helpers.
Model architecture changes or retraining; we only route to existing verified model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Flag creation: ops can create/target a tenant-level feature flag that toggles unified endpoint routing.
SDK opt-in: Node/Python/Go SDKs expose a single boolean to opt client traffic into the new surface; examples documented.
Behavior parity: for 95% of eval prompt-set responses, generation token distributions do not diverge >5% from baseline for the first month of canary traffic.
Latency SLO: p95 latency delta for flagged traffic must remain within +30ms of baseline for the canary cohort.
Cost ceiling: per-token unit cost increase for flagged traffic must not exceed configured threshold (default 12%) during canary.
Canary controls: ops can set percent, region, and tenant selectors and adjust in real-time without deploys.
Rollback automation: at least three metrics (error rate, eval-regression, cost) configurable to trigger auto-rollback to pre-flag routing.
Operational playbook: runbook created with steps for increment, validation, rollback and communication to customer success/SEs.
Docs & migration guide: step-by-step migration guide, public changelog note, and sample code in docs site.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature flag infra and SDK hooks merged behind dev-only flags; unit+integration tests green.
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for Redwood internal tenant; run synthetic evals and perf benchmarks for 48 hours.
Phase 2 (customer pilot): opt-in for 3 pilot customers across different traffic patterns (chat-heavy, embedding-heavy, rerank-heavy) for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual roll): increase to 10%, 25%, 50% over weekly windows with evaluation runs at each step and gate checks.
Phase 4 (GA): flip default to new surface for new projects while preserving opt-out for legacy clients for 30 days before deprecation notice.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Per-flag metrics: requests, errors, p50/p95 latency, per-token cost, model response length distribution.
Quality signal: daily eval-run against gold prompt suite with difference report and drift alerts.
End-to-end traces: capture routing hop, kernel variant, batch size distribution for flagged vs baseline traffic.
Alert thresholds: error rate >2x baseline for 5m, eval-quality drop >5% on key prompts, cost increase >15% sustained for 1h.
Dashboard: rollout dashboard with canary cohort breakdown, health indicators, and link to active feature-flag config.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: behavioral regressions visible to customers. Mitigation: conservative pilot selection and eval gating before wider exposure.
Risk: SDK opt-in adoption lags. Mitigation: provide client migration helpers, automated tests, and follow-up developer sessions with pilot customers.
Risk: spike in GPU usage/cost. Mitigation: pre-provisioned dedicated capacity for pilots and throttling policy enforced per-tenant.
Risk: feature flag misconfiguration. Mitigation: change controls, QA of flag targeting, and audit logs with quick rollback toggle.
decisions: Decision 2026-02-28: use percent-based canary flags at the gateway level rather than per-model weight splits to simplify rollback.
Decision 2026-03-03: include client SDK opt-in only for GA; pilot customers will use server-side flag management first.
Decision 2026-03-05: initial eval suite will be a superset of existing hosted evals with added rerank-specific probes.
